review_notes: I read the whole file and the related definitions in EndpointGeometry, SiblingIncidenceLedger, SiblingIncidence and RowColumnRescue. The file has no simp attributes of its own. The three slack definitions are plain defs that are unfolded by hand with `simp only [...]`, and I don't think they should be made simp, because that would expand them everywhere. The one concrete gap I found is that no canonical simp lemma expresses the norms of `redDisplacement` and `bluePullback` as root distances. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about loops or simplifier behavior. I also did not count every duplicate of the helper facts across the library, so the number of affected files is uncertain beyond RowColumnRescue.

findings.excerpt:
have hr₁ : ‖configuration.redDisplacement .left‖ =
      dist (configuration .red .root) (configuration .red .left) := by
    simp [SixPointConfiguration.redDisplacement, dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev]
findings.problem: `redDisplacement` and `bluePullback` are plain defs with no simp lemmas, so their norms have no canonical form. Here the proof re-proves four facts `‖redDisplacement ℓ‖ = dist (red root) (red ℓ)` and `‖bluePullback ℓ‖ = dist (blue root) (blue ℓ)`, each by unfolding the def and running ad hoc `simp`. Each fact is then used by `rw [← hr₁, ...]` in the reverse direction, because `simp only` cannot rewrite the norms by itself. The same facts are re-proved as `hb₁dist`, `hb₂dist`, `hr₁dist` and `hr₂dist` in RowColumnRescue (using `simp [...]` or `rw [SixPointConfiguration.redDisplacement, norm_sub_rev, dist_eq_norm]`). The only general lemmas, `incidenceChildRadius_red_eq_norm` and `incidenceChildRadius_blue_eq_norm`, are stated for `incidenceChildRadius` at `incidenceChild child`, not for an arbitrary label. They are also not simp. Different call sites therefore get different normal forms for the same quantity.
findings.proposed_change: In EndpointGeometry, next to `dist_redDisplacement` and `dist_bluePullback`, add two general lemmas. The first is `norm_redDisplacement (configuration) (label) : ‖configuration.redDisplacement label‖ = dist (configuration .red .root) (configuration .red label)`. The second is `norm_bluePullback (configuration) (label) : ‖configuration.bluePullback label‖ = dist (configuration .blue .root) (configuration .blue label)`. Tag both `@[simp]`, with the norm on the left and the distance on the right. The orientation is safe: the distance form is the one that appears in `matchedChildAverage`, `thirdActiveFailureSlack` and the other slack definitions, and the right-hand sides contain no `redDisplacement` or `bluePullback`, so nothing can rewrite back. Then delete hr₁, hr₂, hb₁ and hb₂ here and in RowColumnRescue, and replace the `rw [← hr₁, ...]` step with `simp only [norm_redDisplacement, norm_bluePullback]` or the same names in the existing `simp` calls.
findings.benefit: Every norm of a red displacement or blue pullback then normalizes to the distance form used throughout the slack definitions. This removes about twelve lines of repeated local proofs and the manual reverse rewrites, and it gives future proofs about these vectors one stated rule instead of copy-pasted unfold-and-simp calls.
